source.section: Form 540 lines 13 to 19 and 31 to 33 (PDF pages 39-40); PDF page 13 Line 18 standard deduction chart and Line 31; PDF page 75 Tax Rate Schedules; Schedule CA (540) line 5 (no adjustment for a private pension, PDF page 60)

worked: Single, 50: wages 80,000 and a private employer pension 30,000; federal AGI = 80,000 + 30,000 = 110,000. Form 540 line 13 federal AGI = 110,000.00. Federal taxable income = 110,000.00 - 15,750.00 federal standard deduction = 94,250.00 (given, not tested; the federal senior deduction is ignored). Subtractions: none (a private pension needs no adjustment on Schedule CA line 5, PDF page 60). Form 540 line 14 = 0.00. Additions (line 16): 0.00. Line 15 = line 17 California AGI = 110,000.00 - 0.00 = 110,000.00. Line 18 California standard deduction (single, PDF page 13 chart) 5,706.00. Line 19 taxable income = 110,000.00 - 5,706.00 = 104,294.00. Tax on 104,294.00 by the projection's brackets: 11,079.00 x 1% = 110.79; 15,185.00 x 2% = 303.70; 15,188.00 x 4% = 607.52; 16,090.00 x 6% = 965.40; 15,182.00 x 8% = 1,214.56; 31,570.00 x 9.3% = 2,936.01; total 6,137.98. Line 31: Tax Rate Schedule X (PDF page 75), from its printed base, gives 6,137.98. Line 32 exemption credits: federal AGI 110,000.00 is not more than 252,203.00, so no AGI limitation; line 7 personal 1 x 153 = 153.00; line 9 senior 0 x 153 = 0.00; line 32 = 153.00. Line 33 = 6,137.98 - 153.00 = 5,984.98; no other credits (lines 34 to 47 nil), line 48 = 5,984.98. State income tax = 5,984.98.
